subject.title: feat: add lease-bound metadata to session spawns

question: Should OpenClaw adopt lease-backed external-orchestrator session control as a permanent core Gateway API, or provide only a generic extension seam for the downstream Agentic OS integration?
rationale: This choice determines the long-term public protocol, persistence, authorization, and ownership boundary; it cannot be resolved safely from tests or patch mechanics alone.

options.title: Require a generic core seam
options.body: Keep only a narrowly reusable authorization and spawn-lifecycle seam in core, then move Agentic OS-specific RPC names, metadata, replay policy, and documentation to the owner integration.

options.title: Sponsor the core protocol
options.body: Accept this as a core public Gateway API and require explicit protocol ownership, compatibility/versioning commitments, upgrade behavior, and security review before merge.

options.title: Keep it downstream
options.body: Retain the existing core surfaces and implement the orchestration contract in the downstream integration unless a concrete missing extension API is identified.

recommendation.title: Require a generic core seam
recommendation.body: Keep only a narrowly reusable authorization and spawn-lifecycle seam in core, then move Agentic OS-specific RPC names, metadata, replay policy, and documentation to the owner integration.

likelyOwner.reason: A current Gateway/session-runtime owner should make the API-boundary decision after history-backed routing identifies the responsible maintainers.
